heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Benin
heroData.subtitle: Hire compliant teams in Benin without a local entity
heroData.description: Employer of Record (EOR) services in Benin allow external companies to hire local talent legally. The EOR acts as the legal employer, handling payroll, taxes, and social security deductions (CNSS) while you manage daily operations.
heroData.bestFor: Companies engaging 1-10 employees for market testing

steps.title: Requirement Gathering
steps.description: Define candidate details, salary (in XOF), and scope of work. Ensure salary meets the minimum wage of 52,000 XOF/month.

steps.title: Contract Generation
steps.description: EOR drafts a local compliant employment contract in French, adhering to Benin's Labor Code (Law No. 98-004). Mandatory clauses include duration, probationary period (1-3 months), and notice periods.

steps.title: Employee Registration
steps.description: EOR registers the employee with the Caisse Nationale de Sécurité Sociale (CNSS) and tax authorities (Direction Générale des Impôts).

steps.title: Onboarding & IT Setup
steps.description: Employee signs the contract. EOR sets up payroll profiles and benefits. Optional equipment provision is arranged.

items.title: Permanent Establishment (PE)
items.text: Long-term use of EOR (12-18+ months) for core revenue-generating roles may trigger PE risks, subjecting the foreign entity to corporate tax.

items.title: Probation Periods
items.text: Probation cannot exceed 3 months for executives and 1 month for other employees, renewable once.

items.title: Fixed-Term Contracts (CDD)
items.text: CDD contracts are limited to 2 years and can be renewed once. Afterward, they automatically convert to indefinite term (CDI).

items.title: Probation (Standard)
items.text: 1 Month (Renewable once)

items.title: Probation (Executives)
items.text: 3 Months (Renewable once)

items.title: Fixed Term (CDD)
items.text: Max 2 Years (Renewable once)

items.title: Notice (Standard)
items.text: 1 Month

items.title: Notice (Executives)
items.text: 3 Months

items.title: Retirement Age
items.text: 60 Years

faqs.question: Can I hire contractors via EOR?
faqs.answer: Yes, but misclassification risk is high. If a contractor works fixed hours under your supervision, they may be deemed an employee by labor inspectors.

faqs.question: What is the notice period for termination?
faqs.answer: 15 days for hourly workers, 1 month for regular employees, and 3 months for executives/supervisors.

faqs.question: Is a 13th-month salary mandatory?
faqs.answer: No, it is not legally required in Benin, but it is a common customary benefit expected by many employees.

steps.title: Data Aggregation
steps.description: Collect timesheets, overtime hours, and bonus data by the 20th of the month. Working week is standard 40 hours.

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Calculation
steps.description: Apply IRPP (Income Tax) rates (0-30%) and CNSS deductions (3.6% employee share).

steps.title: Payslip Distribution
steps.description: Distribute payslips to employees (electronic or paper) by the 25th-30th. Must be in French.

steps.title: Remittance
steps.description: Pay net salaries to employees. Remit taxes (IRPP) and social security (CNSS) contributions by the 10th of the following month.

items.title: Minimum Wage
items.text: As of 2025, the minimum wage (SMIG) is 52,000 XOF per month.

items.title: VPS Tax
items.text: Employers must pay a Versement Patronal sur Salaires (VPS) of 4% on gross salaries, remitted quarterly.

items.title: Overtime Rates
items.text: 12% premium for 41-48 hours, 35% for beyond 48 hours. Night work and holidays command higher premiums (50-100%).

items.title: New Year's Day
items.text: January 1

items.title: Vodoun Festival
items.text: January 10 - Unique to Benin

items.title: Easter Monday
items.text: Variable (April)

items.title: Labour Day
items.text: May 1

items.title: Ascension Day
items.text: Variable (May)

items.title: Whit Monday
items.text: Variable (June)

items.title: Independence Day
items.text: August 1

items.title: Assumption
items.text: August 15

items.title: All Saints' Day
items.text: November 1

items.title: Christmas Day
items.text: December 25

faqs.question: What is VPS?
faqs.answer: The Versement Patronal sur Salaires is a 4% payroll tax paid by the employer on gross salaries.

faqs.question: Are benefits taxable?
faqs.answer: Yes, cash allowances (housing, transport) are generally taxable. In-kind benefits are also valued and taxed.

faqs.question: When is the payroll tax due?
faqs.answer: Remittances for CNSS and IRPP must be made by the 10th of the following month.

faqs.question: When are tax returns due?
faqs.answer: Monthly declarations for IRPP and CNSS are due by the 10th of the following month. Annual summaries are due by April 30th.

faqs.question: Is severance pay mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, for dismissal without gross misconduct. Rates start at 30% of monthly salary per year for the first 5 years.

faqs.question: What currency must be used?
faqs.answer: Salaries must be paid in West African CFA Francs (XOF), though executive contracts can reference foreign currency equivalents.

steps.title: Enter Gross Salary
steps.description: Input the monthly gross salary in XOF.

steps.title: Select Tax Class
steps.description: Choose resident or non-resident status for accurate IRPP.

steps.title: Add Allowances
steps.description: Include taxable and non-taxable allowances (transport, housing).

steps.title: Calculate
steps.description: View the breakdown of Employer Cost, Employee Deductions, and Net Pay.

faqs.question: Does this include all taxes?
faqs.answer: These rates cover standard social security and income taxes. Specific sector levies or union dues are excluded.

faqs.question: How is the Taxable Base calculated?
faqs.answer: Taxable Income = Gross Salary - Social Security (3.6%) - Professional Expenses Deduction (varies).

faqs.question: Are bonuses taxed?
faqs.answer: Yes, bonuses are generally part of taxable income and subject to CNSS and IRPP.

items.title: Family Quotient
items.text: IRPP is reduced based on number of dependent children. The reduction reduces the tax payable.

items.title: Rounding
items.text: Tax calculations often round down to the nearest 1,000 XOF in practice.

items.title: Total Cost
items.text: Total Employer Cost = Gross Salary + ~20.4% (CNSS + VPS).

items.title: Payslip
items.text: Mandatory monthly. Must show gross, deductions, and net.

items.title: Payment Mode
items.text: Bank transfer is standard for formal employees. MoMo is used for informal/casual labor.

items.title: Late Payment
items.text: Salaries must be paid at regular intervals (usually monthly). Late payments can trigger labor disputes.

heroData.title: Incorporation in Benin
heroData.subtitle: Setup your SARL or Branch in Benin
heroData.description: Establish a legal presence in Benin. The Limited Liability Company (SARL) is the most common structure for foreign investors, governed by OHADA business laws.

steps.title: Capital Deposit
steps.description: Deposit minimum share capital (theoretically 1 XOF, practically 1M XOF favored for credibility) in a local bank account.

steps.title: Notarization
steps.description: Draft Articles of Association and have them notarized. This is mandatory for incorporation.

steps.title: Registration (GUFE)
steps.description: Submit documents to the Guichet Unique de Formalisation des Entreprises (GUFE). Register with the Commercial Registry (RCCM).

steps.title: Tax & Social Security
steps.description: Obtain IFU (Tax ID) and register with CNSS for social security. Obtain the Carte Professionnelle de Commerçant.

steps.title: Parent Company Docs
steps.description: Provide certified copies of the parent company's Articles of Association and Board Resolution authorizing the branch.

steps.title: Registration
steps.description: Register with the RCCM at the Commercial Court. The branch is not a separate legal entity.

steps.title: Validity Period
steps.description: Note that branches are valid for 2 years, renewable once by Ministry of Trade authorization. Conversion to SARL is eventually required.

items.title: SARL (LLC)
items.text: Most common. No minimum capital legally required by OHADA (1 XOF), but 1,000,000 XOF often recommended by banks. Liability limited to contributions.

items.title: SA (Public Ltd)
items.text: Minimum capital 10,000,000 XOF. Auditor required. Suited for large enterprises needing to raise public capital.

items.title: Branch Office
items.text: Can only operate for 2 years. Must convert to a local subsidiary significantly afterwards unless a special waiver is granted.

items.title: Hierarchy
items.text: Business structures are hierarchical. Decisions come from the top. Address counterparts with formal titles (Monsieur/Madame).

items.title: Greetings
items.text: Handshakes are common. Take time to inquire about health and family before talking business.

items.title: Punctuality
items.text: Punctuality is expected of foreigners, though meetings may start late. Patience is a virtue.

faqs.question: Can foreigners own 100% of a company?
faqs.answer: Yes, 100% foreign ownership is permitted in most sectors in Benin.

faqs.question: Is a physical office required?
faqs.answer: Yes, a registered office address in Benin is required for the RCCM registration. Virtual offices are sometimes accepted but scrutinized.

faqs.question: Do I need a resident director?
faqs.answer: No, directors can be foreign nationals and non-residents, but they must obtain a residency card if they plan to live in Benin.

heroData.title: Talent Acquisition in Benin
heroData.subtitle: Recruit top talent in Cotonou and beyond
heroData.description: Find skilled professionals in Benin. Recruitment agencies typically charge 10-30% of annual salary. French is the primary business language.

steps.title: Sourcing
steps.description: Leverage local job boards, LinkedIn, and agencies. Primary language for listings is French.

steps.title: Screening
steps.description: Interview candidates. Verify language proficiency (French/English) and technical skills.

steps.title: Verification
steps.description: Conduct background checks (criminal record, education) with candidate consent. Medical exam required for some roles.

steps.title: Offer
steps.description: Extend offer letter detailing gross salary in XOF. Upon acceptance, sign formal employment contract.

items.title: Language Skills
items.text: While French is official, many tech professionals speak English, but validation is needed.

items.title: Labor Quotas
items.text: Priority must often be given to nationals. Work permits for foreigners are only granted if no local talent is available.

items.title: Background Checks
items.text: Criminal records (Casier Judiciaire) can be requested from the court. Consent is mandatory.

items.title: Tech Hubs
items.text: Cotonou is the economic center. Sèmè City is an emerging innovation campus aiming to train tech talent.

items.title: Education
items.text: University of Abomey-Calavi is the largest, producing graduates in sciences and law.

items.title: Employment Contracts
items.text: Written contracts are mandatory for fixed-term roles. Oral contracts differ but written is best practice.

faqs.question: Is English widely spoken?
faqs.answer: French is the business language. English proficiency is growing in tech but not guaranteed.

faqs.question: How long is the hiring process?
faqs.answer: Typically 4-6 weeks from posting to offer acceptance.

faqs.question: Are 13th month salaries mandatory?
faqs.answer: No, but they are a very common custom and expected by most white-collar employees.

heroData.title: HRIS Solutions in Benin
heroData.subtitle: Digitize your HR operations
heroData.description: Adopting HRIS in Benin helps in managing payroll compliance, especially with complex tax brackets and social security splits.

items.title: Global Players
items.text: Sage HR, Odoo, and Zoho People are widely used due to their flexibility and localization modules.

items.title: Regional Solutions
items.text: HRMSJoy, MenaPAY, and Quick Payroll offer specific African payroll compliance features.

items.title: Localization
items.text: Ensure the system supports XOF currency and French language interface for local staff.

steps.title: Requirements Mapping
steps.description: Identify needs: Payroll (CNSS/IRPP), Leave Management, Performance Tracking.

steps.title: Configuration
steps.description: Set up statutory tax rules. Configure 1.5% - 4% industrial injury rates based on risk.

steps.title: Data Migration
steps.description: Import employee data. Ensure GDPR and local data law compliance (APDP).

steps.title: Training & Go-Live
steps.description: Train HR and employees on self-service portals. Parallel run payroll for 1 month.

items.title: APDP Registration
items.text: Data controllers processing personal data must register with the APDP (Autorité de Protection des Données Personnelles).

items.title: Data Sovereignty
items.text: Cross-border data transfer rules apply. Ensure cloud providers have adequate protection clauses.

items.title: Record Retention
items.text: Payroll and personnel records should be kept for at least 5-10 years for tax and labor audits.

faqs.question: Are electronic payslips legal?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the employee consents and the integrity of the document is guaranteed.

faqs.question: Can I pay salaries in foreign currency?
faqs.answer: Generally, local salaries must be paid in XOF. Expats may have split payroll arrangements subject to specific rules.

faqs.question: Is cloud storage allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes, but if data is hosted abroad, you must notify APDP and ensure the host country has adequate privacy laws.

heroData.title: Accounting in Benin
heroData.subtitle: SYSCOHADA Standards and Financial Reporting
heroData.description: Benin follows the OHADA accounting system (SYSCOHADA). Strict compliance with annual filings and statutory audits is required for certain entities.

steps.title: Bookkeeping
steps.description: Maintain daily records in accordance with SYSCOHADA. Fiscal year is Jan 1 to Dec 31.

steps.title: Financial Statements
steps.description: Prepare Balance Sheet, Income Statement, Cash Flow Statement (new in revised SYSCOHADA), and Notes by March 31.

steps.title: Audit (If applicable)
steps.description: Statutory auditor reviews accounts. Mandatory for SA and large SARLs (Capital > 10M XOF or Turnover > 250M XOF).

steps.title: Filing
steps.description: File tax returns and financial statements by April 30. Submit to Commercial Registry by July 15.

items.title: SYSCOHADA
items.text: The mandatory accounting framework. Differs from IFRS but converged in some areas recently.

items.title: IFRS
items.text: Required for listed companies and those making public calls for capital. Optional for SMEs alongside SYSCOHADA.

items.title: Language
items.text: All accounting records and statutory filings must be in French.

items.title: March 31
items.text: Deadline to prepare annual financial statements.

items.title: April 30
items.text: Deadline for CIT balance payment and tax return filing.

items.title: July 15
items.text: Deadline to deposit financial statements at the court registry.

faqs.question: Can I use English for accounting?
faqs.answer: No, French is the mandatory language for all legal and accounting documents in Benin.

faqs.question: Do I need a local accountant?
faqs.answer: It is highly recommended to engage a local 'Expert Comptable' registered with the OECCA-Benin.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for late filing?
faqs.answer: Penalties include fines and interest on unpaid taxes, typically starting at 10% and scaling up.

steps.title: Corporate Filings
steps.description: Verify annual return submission and trade register (RCCM) updates.

steps.title: Labor Compliance
steps.description: Check employment contracts, CNSS monthly filings, and workplace safety registers.

steps.title: Tax Compliance
steps.description: Valid Tax Clearance Certificate (Quitus Fiscal) is often needed for tenders and imports.

steps.title: Data Privacy
steps.description: Ensure registration with APDP if processing personal data. Update privacy policies.

items.title: Anti-Money Laundering
items.text: Strict AML laws (CENTIF) apply. Banks conduct rigorous KYB/KYC. Reporting suspicious transactions is mandatory.

items.title: UBO Register
items.text: Ultimate Beneficial Owner disclosure is required during incorporation and banking setup.

items.title: Sector Licenses
items.text: Verify if your industry (e.g., Telecom, Banking, Mining) needs specific ministry approvals.

items.title: Law No. 2017-20
items.text: Governs personal data protection. Aligned with GDPR principles. Consent is the primary legal basis.

items.title: Penalties
items.text: Non-compliance with APDP can result in heavy fines and imprisonment.

items.title: E-Signatures
items.text: Electronic signatures are legally recognized under the Digital Code.

items.title: CNSS
items.text: National Social Security Fund - Labor benefits.

items.title: DGI
items.text: General Directorate of Taxes - Tax administration.

items.title: APDP
items.text: Data Protection Authority - Privacy oversight.

faqs.question: How often is the UBO register updated?
faqs.answer: Must be updated within 30 days of any change in ownership structure.

faqs.question: Can I have foreign directors?
faqs.answer: Yes, foreign directors are permitted and do not need to be shareholders.

faqs.question: Is insurance mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, professional civil liability insurance is mandatory for certain regulated professions.

steps.title: Registration
steps.description: Obtain IFU (Identifiant Fiscal Unique) upon incorporation.

steps.title: Monthly Declarations
steps.description: File VAT, payroll taxes (IRPP, VPS), and WHT by the 10th of each month.

steps.title: Provisional CIT
steps.description: Pay CIT in 4 installments throughout the year based on previous year's tax.

steps.title: Annual Finalization
steps.description: File annual return by April 30 and pay outstanding balance. Minimum tax is 1.5% of turnover.

items.title: Investment Code
items.text: Specific incentives exist for investments in industrial, agricultural, and tourism sectors, offering tax holidays.

items.title: Transfer Pricing
items.text: Benin enforces transfer pricing regulations. Documentation is required for transactions with related parties.

items.title: Treaties
items.text: Benin has limited Double Tax Treaties (France, WAEMU countries). Verify applicability to reduce WHT.

items.title: e-Services
items.text: The DGI has modernized with an online portal (e-impot) for declarations and payments.

items.title: Tax Audits
items.text: Audits can be frequent. Maintaining impeccable records for 10 years is critical defense.

items.title: Quitus Fiscal
items.text: A Tax Clearance Certificate is essential for government tenders and importing goods.

faqs.question: What is the VAT registration threshold?
faqs.answer: Generally, all businesses conducting commercial activity must register. There's no effective 'small business' exemption for VAT on imports.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum tax?
faqs.answer: Yes, companies making a loss must still pay a minimum tax of 0.75% to 1.5% of turnover, depending on the sector.

faqs.question: Are digital services taxed?
faqs.answer: Yes, 18% VAT applies to digital services supplied by non-residents.

heroData.title: Master Service Agreements
heroData.subtitle: Contracting in Benin
heroData.description: Drafting enforceable MSAs and contracts in Benin requires adherence to the Civil Code and commercial laws.

steps.title: Governing Law
steps.description: Explicitly state Benin Law (or OHADA Uniform Acts) as governing. Civil Code principles apply.

steps.title: Language
steps.description: Draft in French. If bilingual, specify which version prevails (usually French in local courts).

steps.title: Dispute Resolution
steps.description: Include an arbitration clause. Cotonou has an arbitration center (CAMA). Arbitration is often faster than courts.

steps.title: Execution
steps.description: Ensure authorized signatories sign. Notarization adds evidentiary weight but is not always mandatory for commercial contracts.

items.title: Payment Terms
items.text: Specify currency (XOF or Foreign). Note that payments abroad may be subject to validation by the Ministry of Finance / BCEAO.

items.title: Force Majeure
items.text: Civil Code recognizes force majeure, but defining specific events (e.g., political unrest, pandemic) reduces ambiguity.

items.title: Liability Caps
items.text: Limitation of liability clauses are generally enforceable, except in cases of gross negligence or willful misconduct.

items.title: Formalities
items.text: Contracts often require seals and initials on every page to be considered fully executed and secure.

items.title: Relationship
items.text: Contracts are seen as the beginning of a relationship. Flexibility is often expected during execution.

items.title: Language
items.text: Always ensure the French version is the master version to avoid interpretation issues in court.

items.title: Registration
items.text: Certain contracts (e.g., leases, large supply contracts) may need registration with tax authorities for validity/enforceability against third parties.

items.title: Stamp Duty
items.text: Stamp duties apply to many legal documents. Rates vary by document type.

items.title: Statute of Limitations
items.text: Commercial claims generally expire after 5 years.

faqs.question: Are digital signatures legal?
faqs.answer: Yes, Benin's Digital Code recognizes electronic signatures, provided they meet security standards.

faqs.question: Can I use foreign law?
faqs.answer: Yes, for international contracts, but mandatory Beninese public policy provisions (public order) will still apply.

faqs.question: How long does litigation take?
faqs.answer: Commercial court cases can take 1-3 years. Arbitration is recommended for efficiency.

heroData.title: Software Development Providers
heroData.subtitle: Tech Ecosystem in Benin
heroData.description: The Beninese tech scene is growing, with firms in Cotonou offering web, mobile, and enterprise software solutions.

items.title: RightCom
items.text: Cloud-based customer experience (CX) software, SaaS, and analytics.

items.title: Benin Digital
items.text: ESN specializing in digital transformation for banking, retail, and industry.

items.title: Albendigitech
items.text: Offers end-to-end solutions: Web design, mobile apps, ERP (Odoo), and digital marketing.

steps.title: Vendor Selection
steps.description: Review portfolios. Many firms are small/medium. Verify capacity for enterprise projects.

steps.title: SOW Definition
steps.description: Define scope clearly. Agile is becoming common but Waterfall is still prevalent.

steps.title: Contracting
steps.description: Sign Service Agreement. Ensure IP transfer clauses are explicit.

steps.title: Kickoff
steps.description: Align on communication tools (Slack/Teams). Set bi-weekly sprints.

items.title: Sèmè City
items.text: The massive innovation and knowledge city project near Cotonou is a hub for startups and R&D.

items.title: Connectivity
items.text: Fiber availability is improving in Cotonou/Porto-Novo via ISOCEL and Benin Telecoms.

items.title: Power Stability
items.text: Power cuts can occur. Ensure your partner has backup power solutions.

faqs.question: What are common tech stacks?
faqs.answer: PHP (Laravel), Java, and Python are popular. Flutter is growing for mobile.

faqs.question: Is IP protection strong?
faqs.answer: Benin is an OAPI member, offering IP protection, but explicit contract clauses transferring IP are essential.

faqs.question: Can I hire remotely?
faqs.answer: Yes, remote work is accepted, but ensure reliable internet and power backup provisions.

heroData.title: Marketing Agencies in Benin
heroData.subtitle: Digital & Creative Services
heroData.description: Reach the Beninese audience through top digital and creative agencies specializing in social media, SEO, and local branding.

items.title: Albendigitech
items.text: Strong in SEO, PPC, and Google Business Profile management.

items.title: EchoHouse
items.text: Regional heavyweight offering 360° creative and digital solutions.

items.title: BSM Groupe
items.text: Located in Abomey-Calavi, focuses on branding, street marketing, and content creation.

steps.title: Audience Research
steps.description: Understanding local demographics. Mobile usage is high (MTN/Moov).

steps.title: Channel Strategy
steps.description: Facebook and WhatsApp are dominant. LinkedIn for B2B. Radio is still vital for mass reach.

steps.title: Content Localization
steps.description: French is key, but local languages (Fon, Yoruba) in audio/video ads boost engagement.

steps.title: Execution
steps.description: Launch ads. Monitor KPIs. Adjust spend based on CPA.

items.title: Mobile First
items.text: Most internet access is via mobile data. Ensure all assets are mobile-optimized.

items.title: Trust
items.text: Beninese consumers value trust and peer recommendations. Influencer marketing is growing.

items.title: Payment Methods
items.text: Mobile Money (MTN MoMo) is the preferred payment method for e-commerce, not cards.

faqs.question: Are there advertising restrictions?
faqs.answer: Yes, strict rules apply to alcohol, tobacco, and pharmaceutical advertising.

faqs.question: What is the best time to post?
faqs.answer: Evenings (7-9 PM) and weekends often see higher engagement on social platforms.

faqs.question: Can I use global influencers?
faqs.answer: Local macro and micro-influencers typically drive better conversion due to relatability.
